item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-05-17
item.description: ## 今日发生了什么 社区今天相当活跃，开发者们推出了多个新项目，包括标准化 UDT 合约套件和论坛桌面小工具 TalkPulse，同时 DAO Treasury 的 ZK 投票方案也在持续推进中。[S04, S05, S08, S02, S03] ## 重点话题 **标准化 UDT 合约套件发布**：开发者 orange-xc 推出了 standard-udt-contracts，一套 CKB 上的标准化 UDT 合约项目，并坦诚说明开发过程中大量使用了 AI 辅助，但核心逻辑和安全边界均经过人工逐项审阅。[S04, S05] **论坛小工具 TalkPulse 亮相**：ArthurZhang 用 Kimi + Codex 进行 vibe coding 实验，打造了一款 macOS 桌面小组件，可在桌面实时显示论坛最新话题、关注关键词和新鲜动态。[S08] **DAO Treasury ZK 投票方案有进展**：chenyukang 分享了基于 ZK 的投票概念验证仓库链接，表示团队倾向这一方向因其简洁且结果可公开验证；社区成员 phroi 对此表示欢迎，认为有代码可看让 ZK 路径更易理解。[S02, S03] **CKBadger 本地浏览器获反馈**：有用户表示很喜欢 CKBadger 的界面，但目前在树莓派上运行尚不稳定；另有社区成员建议官方团队应托管维护该项目，与外观多年未变的官方浏览器并行。[S06, S07] **CKBoost 社区 engagement 平台进入实测**：Alive24 发布产品交付报告，CKBoost 已从提案概念推进到 CKB...

item.title: A New Chapter for CKB: Introducing the Common Knowledge Base Association (1 posts)
item.description: I wanted to sign up. However, I was unable to create a Google account. The process requires scanning (with a mobile device) a QR code displayed on the screen during registration. I believe this (proprietary?) solution poses a hurdle for some users. Would a decentralized solution—one not dependent on centralized, monopolistic tech giants—be feasible? For the time being, I am refraining from registering the address CKBA.bit.cc or similar, but I would like to highlight and promote permissionless options, and—as long as the current solution remains in a state that I find unsatisfactory—I will, unfortunately, refrain from joining. A long-time loyal supporter.

item.title: TalkPulse: a small vibe-coded experiment with Kimi + Codex (1 posts)
item.description: Hi, community I’ve been experimenting with vibe coding using Kimi + Codex, and ended up building a small macOS desktop widget called TalkPulse. image776×780 74.9 KB The idea is simple: keep recent community forum topics, watch keywords, and fresh activity visible on the desktop, so you don’t have to keep the forum open all day. You can glance at it, see what’s new, and click straight into the discussion. This is not meant to be a serious polished product. It’s more of a small experimental tool for people to play with, fork, modify, or critique. One interesting takeaway from the process: Kimi’s review ability is surprisingly strong. It caught a lot of UI/UX issues and subtle logic problems...

item.title: CKB probably isn’t the first chain most people learn, but it might be the first one that makes them rethink what a blockchain is for (1 posts)
item.description: Most people discovering CKB are not starting from zero, they’re arriving from Solana, Ethereum, Bitcoin, or somewhere else with assumptions already baked in. That makes the learning experience different. You’re not just learning CKB, you’re unlearning habits from other ecosystems and comparing tradeoffs in real time. I’m curious: what chain did you come from, and what was the hardest mental shift when you started trying to understand CKB?

item.title: DAO Structures and the future of Ai agents (aspirational piece) (2 posts)
item.description: I agree that Ai agents crowd out intrinsic motivation. The whole system in effect could become impersonal as a result. In the grand scheme of things for delegated voting, it doesn’t take too long to make a vote count by humans. It would probably cut down the personal engagement on the whole forum as agents wouldn’t be typically expressing their reasons why they vote or didn’t vote for the proposal. Less epistemic value to debate actually makes the whole system too ‘robotic’. It only sounds logical if you decided to move away without any internet access and the agent voted in your absence. Yes voter fatigue will not be solved that’s for sure. Not everyone feels the need to talk or explain...

item.title: Groth16-ckb: an on-chain Groth16 verifier for CKB-VM (1 posts)
item.description: Gm!gm! I’ve been building groth16-ckb, a general-purpose Groth16 zkSNARK verifier that runs as a CKB-VM type script.
